goals.primary: Stay healthy to the start line

zones.easy: 130-145 (9:00-10:00); avg to 152 in heat through wk11
zones.threshold: 155-164. Used this cycle in week 12 only, as 3 x 0.5 mi at 7:45 with easy floats. Week 8's planned exposure was dropped when the Italy flight settled on Tuesday evening Aug 25: any session early that week would have its 48-hour verdict land mid-transatlantic, where flight swelling and stiffness make the morning check unreadable, so it would have carried flare-band risk for data that had to be discarded. Week 12 therefore becomes the first and only 7:45 exposure, and runs at the shorter 0.5 mi rep length rather than 0.75, holding rep length at the week 4 value so pace is the only variable that moves. Reps should average 158-165; a rep AVERAGING above 164 means the session went above threshold and should be stopped. 7:45 is the threshold pace here because 8:00-8:15 sits only 15-30 sec/mi off MP 8:30 and is not a distinct stimulus. The 164 anchor comes from the Apr 2025 Jersey City Half (162 avg) and is 15 months old; re-anchor off the Sep 19 check.
zones.vo2: 164+ Short reps of 0.25 mi at 7:00-7:15 (week 7, Aug 18) sit in this pace territory but not in its duration; at 1:45-1:49 per rep they never reach steady state, so they carry no HR gate and are judged on split averages and the morning-after only.

tibRules: Flare trigger is SUSTAINED fast pace in the 7:30-7:45 band, not volume or consecutive days. This block deliberately tests the top edge of that band: week 12 prescribes 7:45 in broken reps with easy floats. Everything else stays clear of it. Verified Jul 29 2026 at 8:00-8:15: fastest 400m 7:51, fastest half mile 7:56, fastest mile 8:18, max HR 162 against a threshold of 164. Week 12 (Tue Sep 22) is now the only 7:45 exposure and the decision point for whether the pace is viable at all; week 8's planned test was dropped because its morning-after verdict would have fallen mid-flight. Week 7's Aug 18 reps run at 7:00-7:15, below the band rather than inside it, and are capped at 0.25 mi.

Tempo sessions run in weeks 4 and 12 only. Week 6's tempo was converted to an easy run on the day (Aug 13) and then skipped outright for inner left knee pain; it is not made up. Week 4 (done) ran at 8:00-8:15 with 8:30 as a bad-day floor. Week 8's tempo was dropped for travel: the Tuesday Aug 25 redeye put its 48-hour verdict mid-transatlantic, where flight swelling makes the morning check unreadable, so the session would have carried flare-band risk for data that had to be discarded. It is not made up either. Week 12 runs at 7:45 unconditionally and is the block's only exposure to that pace. Rep length progresses 3 x 0.5 (wk 4, at 8:00-8:15) -> 3 x 0.5 (wk 12, at 7:45): rep length holds while pace rises, one variable at a time. The 0.75 mi reps originally planned for week 12 are dropped along with the week 8 session that would have justified them. Mile reps at 7:45 are deliberately absent from this block. Pace creep is the primary risk; a rep split under 7:38 invalidates the session as a data point. Placement: Wednesday in week 4, Tuesday in week 12 so recovery falls directly after. The week 7 Tuesday interval session is not a tempo and does not change this: short reps below the flare band, not sustained work inside it.

Marathon pace 8:30 is the race-specific workhorse and sits 45-60 sec clear of the flare band, which makes added MP volume the cheapest way to add quality. It appears in long-run pace-up segments throughout and in one midweek session, week 13 Wednesday. Dedicated threshold work exists this cycle but only in week 12.

Fast bursts are safe but never sprint-fast. Strides (<=20s) run twice weekly throughout. Week 7 (Aug 18) extends this to 4 x 0.25 mi at 7:00-7:15, roughly 1:45-1:49 per rep, which is the first sub-7:30 running of the block. The band sits deliberately below the 7:30-7:45 flare band rather than inside it; a 7:15-7:45 band was considered and rejected because its top half is the flare band and it would preview the week 12 session. Rep count, not pace, is the dial if a session feels like too much. Short reps carry no HR gate: they never reach steady state and the watch is unreliable for intervals.

Long-run pace-up segments are capped at MP (8:30) for their sustained blocks, and from week 7 each long run reaches that block through a descending ramp that converts easy miles already sitting in front of it. The ramp is shaping, not added dose: every MP dose and every long-run distance in this file is unchanged by it. Ramp floor is 8:20 with a hard stop at 8:15 on any split, which keeps it 30-plus seconds clear of the flare band; judged on split averages after the fact, never on the watch. The ramp is the first thing dropped if the knee or tib speaks, and the MP block the second. Sep 19 carries no ramp: it is a measurement, and a ramp in front of it would change what is being measured. Week 8's long run carries neither ramp nor MP; altitude makes both meaningless.

At most one dedicated fast session per week, counting tempo and midweek MP alike, and at most one MP dose within that week's long run. A dose may be delivered as one continuous block or as two blocks separated by an easy float; the broken format is a way of delivering the same dose with less continuous time under tension, not a way of taking two doses. Floats within a long run run at full easy pace, 9:00-10:00; a float run faster than that turns the whole span into a continuous progression run and voids the distinction. Week 9 carries no quality at all and week 8's long run carries none either; both are travel weeks and that is intentional. Week 7 was originally in that group and now carries two quality items, intervals on Aug 18 and a ramp-plus-MP long run on Aug 22. This is a recorded exception to the one-fast-session-per-week rule rather than a silent break: it was flagged and taken deliberately. With week 8's tempo dropped, those intervals no longer sit anywhere near a 7:45 test, so the blur they risked never materialized. Week 10 was considered as a home for the relocated 7:45 exposure and rejected: its Saturday already carries a ramp-plus-MP long run, and a second recorded exception in one block would be the rule eroding rather than bending.
Morning-after check (touch-tenderness + stairs, for both knee and tib) governs progression, not in-run feel.

Instantaneous watch readings are not evidence, for pace or for HR. Watch pace reads fast during efforts and swings hard: the Jul 29 2026 session logged a 5:58 max speed that never happened, and a perceived 7:30 turned out to be 7:56 on the splits. HR behaves the same way; the Jul 25 2026 long run peaked at 168 while averaging 152.7 at a genuinely easy 9:34 pace. Judge both from run averages and lap splits after the fact, never from the number on the wrist mid-run. Momentary HR spikes cresting a hill carry no information.

Heat and humidity drift HR upward at unchanged pace, and that drift is real cardiovascular strain rather than a measurement error, so the correct response is to slow down, not to work harder. Through week 11, long-run HR may average 150-157 on easy portions and up to 160 within MP segments, and easy weekday runs may average to 152. These are averages across the run, not spot ceilings. Abort gate: if a run's full average exceeds 158 at easy pace, conditions are winning; shorten it or slow it rather than pushing through.

The 164 LT anchor comes from the Apr 2025 Jersey City Half (162 avg) and is about fifteen months old. The Jul 25 2026 easy long run peaked at 168, which means either the anchor has moved or the optical sensor spikes; both are plausible. Every HR zone in this plan inherits that uncertainty. Re-anchor off the Sep 19 sustainability check, which is already built to measure it, and do not widen any HR allowance on the strength of the current number before then.

Altitude changes what the numbers mean. Week 8 Thu-Sun sits at roughly 1,800-2,000m at Alpe di Siusi, which costs about 6 to 8 percent of aerobic capacity, so the same effort buys a pace 20 to 40 sec/mi slower and HR runs high at any given pace. Up there, run by HR and effort and disregard pace targets entirely; do not treat the slower number as lost fitness, and do not chase it back. This is the same logic as the heat rule: real physiological strain, met by slowing down rather than working harder. MP targets are meaningless at altitude and no MP is prescribed there. The first two to four days are the worst of it; the week 8 long run now falls on Sun Aug 30, day five up, which is marginally easier rather than a reason to run it harder. Descending is the part that carries tendon risk: controlled, shorter stride, quicker cadence, no braking. Hiking at altitude is cross-training and is logged separately from mileage; it buys aerobic work and time on feet but not running-specific mechanical loading, so it supplements an easy run rather than replacing one, and lifts are taken downhill wherever offered because descent is the part that carries tendon cost.

structure.Build: Weeks 6-11 (Aug 10 - Sep 20): 22.5 -> 35.5 mpw, dipping to 21.0 in the wk9 travel cutback. Trimmed roughly 5 percent block-wide in mid-August after a skipped run for inner left knee pain; the cuts come out of midweek volume and out of week 8, never out of the three measurement or race-specific long runs. Volume sits in midweek rather than in longer long runs. Week 8's tempo was dropped when the Italy flight settled on Tuesday evening Aug 25, since its 48-hour verdict would have fallen mid-flight; week 6's was skipped outright for knee pain. Neither is made up, which leaves the Build phase with no threshold work at all and pushes the block's only 7:45 exposure to wk 12. Week 8's long run moved from Sat Aug 29 to Sun Aug 30, is at altitude in the Dolomites and carries no MP; the week total is unchanged at 27.0. Week 9's Monday Aug 31 run was cancelled outright and not made up, with 0.5 mi added to Tue Sep 1 and 1.0 mi added to Sat Sep 5, taking wk9 from 24.0 to 21.0 and making the step into wk10 about +48 percent. Week 7's Aug 22 long run gained a 2-mile MP dose so the gap between Aug 15 and Sep 12 does not run four weeks. Week 7 also carries the block's only short-interval session, 4 x 0.25 mi at 7:00-7:15 on Aug 18. LR 12.5 -> 18.
structure.Peak: Weeks 12-14 (Sep 21 - Oct 11): 40 -> 43 mpw with a long-run unload at wk13 (36 mpw, LR 14.5). LR 20 / 14.5 / 22, the 22 on Oct 10. Peak trimmed from 46 to 43; the three long runs of 18 or more survive intact, as do all their MP doses, because peak weekly volume is the cheapest thing to give back and the least expensive in fitness terms. Tempo in wk12 only, on Tuesday, and it is the block's only 7:45 exposure, run as 3 x 0.5 mi rather than the 3 x 0.75 originally planned; wk14 carries none. Wk13 holds the block's only midweek MP session, and its midweek volume keeps the step into wk14 at about +19 percent.
structure.Taper: Weeks 15-17 (Oct 12 - Nov 1): volume drops to 30/24, then race week (~38 incl. race), short MP (8:30) touches to stay sharp, race Nov 1
